audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 with 51.48% over 305 games. The chart gives Irelia 4 stages, Skill 3, Trundle 0 across both layers and win[N] matches phases[N].side row for row, which is also what the mirror audit (audits/top/trundle__irelia.json) records from his side. No chart edit proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trundle's spikes are named but never timed, so 'wait out his R' has no number attached to it.
audit.why: Subjugate is 120/100/80s, Pillar of Ice 21/19.5/18/16.5/15s, Frozen Domain 18/17/16/15/14s, Chomp a flat 3.5s. The 120s rank-1 Subjugate is the whole reason his level-6 window is a window and not a state.

sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json Q, W, E, R cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia is credited with armour shred in four places — whys[3] 'armor-shredding passive', mid 'your Bladesurge passive is shredding his armor', late 'heals him through your armor-shred', whys[6] 'heals through your shred', spikes[3] 'out-sustains your armor-shred'. Ionian Fervor does not shred armour.
audit.why: Riot text for Ionian Fervor: 'When Irelia strikes enemies with spells she gains stacking bonus Attack Speed. At maximum stacks she also gains bonus damage on hit.' Nothing in Irelia's kit reduces armour. Against Trundle this is not a cosmetic error: it invites the reader to skip Grievous Wounds because they believe a shred is already answering his sustain. The mirror audit flagged the identical claim from his side.
audit.corrected: Replaced every shred reference with attack speed / max-stack on-hit damage, and pointed the sustain answer at Grievous Wounds instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trundle's E is called 'Pillar of Filth' in whys[3], mid and wants.foe[1] — the packet flagged one instance, there are three.
audit.why: Riot's name for the ability is Pillar of Ice. The same fields also claim it 'body-blocks your Bladesurge dash'. Bladesurge is a target-selected dash to a unit, and neither the kit files nor the missing-interactions entry for this pairing lists dash-denial here, so the mirror deliberately left that unasserted. I state only what Pillar demonstrably does: it is impassable terrain that takes away the minion you wanted to reset onto.
audit.corrected: Corrected the name in all three fields and reframed the threat as reset-target denial rather than dash-blocking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is described purely as an AD steal; its auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: The derived flags on Trundle's Q list autoReset alongside slow. On a 3.5s cooldown that reset is what makes his burst arrive early inside a trade — the tell is the auto wind-up, not the cast, which changes when you step back.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0] around the reset tell and the 3.5s cycle.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names anti-heal, despite Trundle having two healing sources and a resistance steal.
audit.why: King's Tribute heals him off every nearby unit death — a full wave in lane — and Frozen Domain increases healing from all sources while he stands on it. Subjugate steals Armor and MR, which is why stacking raw resistances is the wrong response and Grievous Wounds is the right one. The full layer already carries Executioner's Calling in report[8]; the content layer contradicted it by implying a shred handled his sustain.
audit.corrected: Named King's Tribute, Frozen Domain and Grievous Wounds in late, whys[6] and spikes[3].

audit.why: No claim proposed about Pillar of Ice denying Bladesurge. Bladesurge is a targeted dash to a unit, the kits do not resolve whether impassable terrain stops it, and the missing-interactions entry for this pairing lists no dash-denial. The mirror left it unasserted for the same reason; both sides now stay silent on it rather than disagreeing.

edits.before: His Chomp (Q) steals your AD and his steady regen keeps him healthy - you have no stun yet, so just farm with Q-resets and stay out of bite range.
edits.after: Chomp (Q) is an auto-attack reset on a 3.5s cooldown that saps your AD - the wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast; farm with Q-resets.

edits.before: Your tightening cooldowns and armor-shredding passive out-trade him here - just track Pillar of Filth (E) so it can't block your dash mid-combo.
edits.after: Your tightening cooldowns and max-stack Ionian Fervor on-hit out-trade him here - track Pillar of Ice (E), 21s at rank 1, and fight while it is down.

edits.after: He out-scales you: a two-item drain-tank heals through your DPS without Grievous Wounds, and Chomp saps your AD, so close before this window.

edits.before: This is your strongest stretch - your Bladesurge passive is shredding his armor and your cooldowns are tight, so chain E-stun into Q-resets and stick to him. The danger is Pillar of Filth (E): he drops it mid-fight to body-block your dash or wall you off the minion you wanted to reset onto, so respect it before you commit. At 6, do NOT facetank Subjugate (R) - it steals your resistances and pours healing into him, flipping an all-in you would otherwise win; bait it or wait it out.
edits.after: This is your strongest stretch - Ionian Fervor at max stacks adds bonus damage on hit and your cooldowns are tight, so chain E-stun into Q-resets and stick to him. The danger is Pillar of Ice (E), 21s at rank 1: he drops it mid-fight to wall you off the minion you wanted to reset onto, so respect it before you commit. At 6, do NOT facetank Subjugate (R) - it steals your resistances and pours healing into him, flipping an all-in you would otherwise win; bait it or wait out its 120 seconds.

edits.before: You don't out-scale a Trundle into the late game - he's a drain-tank who reclaims the two-item window outright. Once he has resists and his R back on a short timer, a straight slugfest heals him through your armor-shred while his Chomp keeps your AD sapped. Your job was the mid-game: snowball lane, take plates and towers on your Trinity Force first-item spike, and force the game to end before his sustain and R turn every extended fight in his favor.
edits.after: You don't out-scale a Trundle into the late game - he's a drain-tank who reclaims the two-item window outright. Once he has resists and his R back on an 80s timer, King's Tribute and Frozen Domain heal him through your DPS unless Grievous Wounds is already on him. Your job was the mid-game: snowball lane, take plates and towers on your first-item spike, and force the game to end before his sustain and R turn every extended fight in his favor.

edits.before: A two-item Trundle out-sustains your armor-shred and his Q keeps your AD sapped, so a straight bruiser slugfest heals him through you - end the game on your mid-game lead first.
edits.after: A two-item Trundle out-sustains you through King's Tribute and Frozen Domain, and Chomp keeps your AD sapped, so buy Grievous Wounds early and end on your mid-game lead.

edits.after: Drop Pillar of Ice (E), up every 21 seconds, to wall you off the minion you wanted to Bladesurge onto

edits.before: Don’t duel in his W — E-stun, shred, and Q-reset out. Irelia wins by trading around Trundle's Subjugate and cashing the pattern: e-stun in, shred, and Q-reset out of his W.
edits.after: Don’t duel on his Frozen Domain — E-stun, burst, Q-reset out. Irelia trades around Subjugate's 120s cooldown and cashes the pattern: stun in, burst, reset out of his W.
